context.title: Cleansing and Restoring
context.summary: A ritual restores a healed person to the community, with two birds, washing, shaving and offerings; then follow rules for mold or 'plague' in houses.
context.background: The ceremony does not heal; it confirms healing that has already happened and welcomes the person back. Jesus tells healed lepers to show themselves to the priest and offer what Moses commanded (Matthew 8:4). The house laws look ahead to life in Canaan (v. 34).

customs.note: One bird was killed over running water; the other was dipped in its blood with cedar, scarlet and hyssop and set free over the open field, a picture of uncleanness carried away.

watchFor: Blood and oil go on the right ear, thumb and toe (vv. 14, 17), as at the priests' ordination.
A cheaper option for the poor (vv. 21–22).
'When ye be come into the land of Canaan' (v. 34).

people.name: Moses
people.summary: Drawn (or Egypt. mesu, “son;” hence Rameses, royal son). On the invitation of Pharaoh (Gen. 45:17-25), Jacob and his sons went down into Egypt.

people.name: Aaron
people.summary: The eldest son of Amram and Jochebed, a daughter of Levi (Ex. 6:20). Some explain the name as meaning mountaineer, others mountain of strength, illuminator.

people.name: Canaan
people.summary: The fourth son of Ham (Gen. 10:6). His descendants were under a curse in consequence of the transgression of his father (9:22-27). His eldest son, Zidon, was the father of the Sidonians and Phoenicians.

places.name: Canaan
places.summary: The country which derived its name from the preceding. The name as first used by the Phoenicians denoted only the maritime plain on which Sidon was built.
